To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a class discovery procedure automatically discovers the distinction between acute lymphoblastic leukemias and acute myeloid leukemias without prior knowledge of the classes; (2) a class predictor derived from the class discovery procedure is able to determine the leukemia class of new leukemia samples; (3) class discovery is based on the assumption that the genes that are differentially expressed between two cancer classes are the genes that have the greatest influence on the difference between the classes.
gene expression profiling can be used to classify acute leukemias into the known classes of acute myeloid leukemias (AML) and lymphoid leukemias.
a generic approach to class discovery and class predication based on gene expression profiling is possible and that it is feasible to use gene expression profiles for cancer classification.

developing new methods and software for the classification and prediction of cancer types based on the analysis of gene expression data.
the discovery of novel molecular signatures of human diseases.
the application of DNA microarray technology for the discovery of new molecular classes in cancer.

we developed a general method for classifying cancers, and we applied this method to acute myeloid leukemias and acute lymphocytic leukemias.
the classification is based on gene expression profiles, the classes are discovered by a clustering algorithm, and the classification of new samples is based on a class predictor.
we have developed a new approach to cancer classification, which is independent of previous biological or medical knowledge and is based on gene expression profiles.

gene expression data can provide useful insights for cancer diagnosis, prognosis and treatment, but the results should be validated using independent data sets and/or by using alternative analytical methods.
